title: Threshold bias of the Maker-Breaker triangle game
premise_risks: The game is often called the 'Chvátal–Erdős triangle game' (person-named object), but the constant question is not a named conjecture
'Improve either bound' form: both directions are hard, but scorer may prefer exact determination
Supporting 2026 budget-variant result is an unrefereed preprint (context only)
plain: On the edges of the complete graph K_n, Maker claims one edge per turn and Breaker claims q edges per turn; Maker wins if she ever owns a triangle. Let q_0(n) be the smallest q for which Breaker wins. It is known that q_0(n) lies between about 1.414 sqrt(n) and 1.633 sqrt(n). What is the right constant, conjecturally sqrt(2)? As a concrete step, can either bound be improved by a constant factor?
math: Let $q_0(n)$ be the least $q$ such that Breaker wins the $(1:q)$ Maker-Breaker triangle game on $E(K_n)$ (Maker first). Known: $(\sqrt2-o(1))\sqrt n\le q_0(n)\le(\sqrt{8/3}+o(1))\sqrt n$. Prove that one of the two bounds can be improved by a constant factor: either there is $c'<\sqrt{8/3}$ with $q_0(n)\le c'\sqrt n$ for all large $n$, or there is $\varepsilon>0$ with $q_0(n)\ge(\sqrt2+\varepsilon)\sqrt n$ for all large $n$.
